articles.title: Who or What? A Continuum for Using AI Wisely
articles.summary: From AI as god to AI as assistant. Here is a continuum of nine roles that can help Christians tell legitimate uses of AI from illegitimate ones, and wise from unwise. See Also A Christian’s Guide to AI Technology is Fast, Sanctification Is Slow, and Claude Can’t Do It For You A La Carte (October 16)
articles.summary_zh: 从AI为神到AI为助手。这里有九个角色的连续体，可以帮助基督徒区分人工智能的合法使用和非法使用，以及明智和不明智的使用。另请参阅基督徒的人工智能指南：人工智能技术快，成圣慢，克劳德无法为你点菜（10 月 16 日）
articles.title_zh: 谁或什么？明智使用人工智能的连续体
articles.content: It is sometimes hard to believe that it has been only four years since AI became widely available. Few technologies have made so massive and rapid a leap into our daily lives, to the extent that AI now exists in the background of all of our lives and, for many of us, in the foreground as well. Few technologies have evolved as quickly, so that the latest ChatGPT model bears about as much resemblance to its debut as the latest MacBook does to a Commodore 64. If all this has happened in just four years, imagine what the next four—or the next fourteen—might hold. As AI’s capabilities have increased, so too have the ways we can use it in our homes, churches, and workplaces. It seems like every month or two we read of a feature that can make a difference to our lives by adding a new ability or taking on work that used to be done by a person. The latest trend is the rise of agents—AI tools like Meta’s Muse or xAI’s Grok Bot that can carry out tasks, routines, and duties on an ongoing basis. With all of the tools available to us and all of their capabilities, it can be difficult to know which uses are legitimate and which are not. We all know that just because AI can do a task doesn’t mean that it should . So how can we determine the legitimate roles AI can play in our lives? I think sketching out a continuum of some of AI’s potential roles can help us. At the beginning are roles that most of us would agree are illegitimate, and at the end roles that most of us would agree are legitimate. Between them are roles that may be illegitimate in some cases and perfectly fine in others. These demand that we approach them thoughtfully to determine whether integrating them into our lives would be an act of wisdom or folly. As you will see, illegitimate roles tend to be those that require a who whereas legitimate roles tend to be those that require a mere what . The Continuum AI as God . There are some people, most of them deeply engaged in the tech industry, who ascribe to AI god-like qualities and who relate to it accordingly. They may believe it is an evil god that is likely to destroy humanity or a benevolent god that is likely to redeem humanity, but in either case, they treat AI as something far more than software. These people go too far and commit idolatry as they attribute to tech what rightly belongs to God. AI as Friend . There are some people who relate to AI as a friend, and even a few troubled people who relate to it as a lover. While AI is capable of mimicking the kind of relationship one might enjoy with a fellow human being, it can only ever mimic it. To relate to AI as a friend is to anthropomorphize a mere technology and worse, to deprive oneself of actual friendship. Though AI can imitate friendship, it cannot be a friend in any legitimate sense of the word, for friendship depends upon personhood. Not only that, but friendship depends upon mutuality and both the blessings and risks that come with relationship. You cannot be friends with AI any more than you can be friends with a tree, a PlayStation, or any other non-being. AI as Counselor . Many people today relate to AI as a counselor—a confidant who will listen patiently and counsel them with a trusted voice. Yet because AI is a what , not a who , it cannot offer answers based on a true understanding of their circumstances, true wisdom that comes from learning and experience, or true compassion that comes from sharing their humanity. It cannot empathize with them, pray for them, or plead with the Holy Spirit for wisdom in helping them. AI is capable of advising in many ways, but not of counseling, for counseling is inherently personal. AI as Pastor . Increasingly, people bring to AI the matters of spiritual health, growth, and well-being that in the past would have been addressed to a pastor. Every Christian needs to be under the loving oversight of a pastor who will care for their soul, and such crucial matters must be entrusted not to AI, but to a pastor who is called and
articles.content_zh:
有时很难相信,自AI广泛提供至今才四年。 很少有技术使我们的日常生活如此巨大和迅速地跃入,以至于AI现在存在于我们所有生活的背景中,对我们许多人来说,也存在于前景中。

很少有技术发展得这么快,因此最新的ChatGPT模型与其首发版的相近程度与最新的MacBook对准将64的相近程度相同. 如果这一切在短短的四年内就发生了,想象下四年,或下十四年可能发生的情况。 随着AI能力的增强,我们在家里、教堂和工作场所使用它的方式也一样。

我们似乎每个月或两个月都读到一个特点,通过增加新的能力或从事过去由一个人完成的工作,可以改变我们的生活。 最近的趋势是,诸如Meta的Muse或xAI的Grok Bot等能够持续执行任务、例行公事和职责的代理-AI工具的兴起。

有了我们可以利用的所有工具及其所有能力,就很难知道哪些用途是合法的,哪些用途不是。 我们都知道, 我们如何确定AI在生活中可以扮演的合法角色? 我认为勾画出AI的一些潜在角色可以帮助我们。

开始时,我们大多数人都认为这种角色是非法的,最后,我们大多数人都认为这种角色是合法的。 两者之间是在某些情况下可能是非法的,而在另一些情况下则完全正确。 这些要求我们深思熟虑地对待他们,以确定将他们融入我们的生活是明智还是愚蠢。

你会看到,非法角色往往是那些需要谁的角色,而合法角色往往是那些只需要什么的角色。 连续AI作为上帝。 有一些人,其中大多数人深入从事技术产业,他们把AI的神性描述为"类似"的特质,并与之相应相通.

他们可能相信是邪恶的神有可能毁灭人性或者仁慈的神有可能赎回人性,但无论在哪种情况下,他们都把AI视为远远超出软件的东西. 这些人太过分了 以偶像为神 因为他们把属于上帝的东西归为技术 作为朋友的AI.

有些人以朋友身份与AI有关,甚至有少数人以恋人身份与之有关系. 虽然AI能够模仿人们可能享受的那种与人类同胞的关系,但它只能模仿它. 作为朋友与AI的关系就是人类化,将一种简单的技术变成更糟糕的技术,剥夺了自己的实际友谊。

虽然大赦国际可以模仿友谊,但它不能是任何合法意义上的朋友,因为友谊取决于人性。 不仅如此,友谊还取决于相互以及关系带来的幸福和风险。 你不可能成为AI的朋友 也不可能成为树上的朋友,PlayStation,或者其他的不幸福. 作为律师的AI.

今天,许多人都把大赦国际当作一个顾问——一个会耐心地倾听他们的意见并以一个值得信赖的声音给他们提供建议的告密者。 然而,由于大赦国际是一个什么人,而不是谁,它不能根据对他们情况的真正理解、来自学习和经验的真正智慧或来自分享其人性的真正同情来提供答案。

它不能同情他们,不能为他们祈祷,也不能恳求圣灵的智慧帮助他们。 大赦国际能够在许多方面提供咨询,但不能提供咨询,因为咨询本质上是针对个人的。 作为牧师的AI. 人们越来越多地将精神健康、成长和福祉等问题带到大赦国际,这些问题过去本来是交给牧师的。

每个基督徒都需要接受一位会关心自己灵魂的牧师的慈爱监督,这种关键事项必须不委托给大赦国际,而委托给一位被叫作"和"和"的牧师".

清晨，遮挡穹顶下方建筑结构的围栏和脚手架被拆除。这座建筑体量庞大，独一无二。人群随即涌来。人们的好奇心并非仅仅源于这位建筑师的名望。这位建筑师年仅34岁，已开始崭露头角，并成为教皇的宠臣。这座巨大的华盖已经成为人们几个月来热议的话题。

articles.title: The Festive Attire We Really Need
articles.summary: Even in our finest clothes we can still be dirty on the inside. Advent reminds us that Jesus dresses us in his righteousness.
articles.summary_zh: 即使穿着我们最好的衣服 内心还是可以脏的 基督提醒我们,耶稣穿戴我们的正义。
articles.title_zh: 我们真正需要的节奏
articles.content: Read He will sit as a refiner and purifier of silver, and he will purify the sons of Levi and refine them like gold and silver, and they will bring offerings in righteousness to the LORD. Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem will be pleasing to the LORD as in the days of old and as in former years. (Mal. 3:3–4) Reflect My grandmother always made going to church a special event. She helped me pick the right dress, made sure my shoes were shiny and clean, and withstood burns from the curling iron to perfect my hairdo. I know church attire can vary. But I still get dressed up for corporate worship because, no matter how cliché it sounds, I want to wear my Sunday best for Jesus. Yet even in our finest clothes, we can still be dirty on the inside. Hidden sins are, after all, hidden. We can sing hymns at max volume, forgetting the way we treated our coworkers last week. We can kneel in prayer, easily dismissing what we posted on the internet earlier that morning. We can take the bread and wine even if we lost it with our kids in the car. People at church only see what’s on the outside, but God looks on the heart (1 Sam. 16:7). And unless we come clean, we can’t come into his presence at all. Even in our finest clothes, we can still be dirty on the inside. Purity in God’s presence is a major theme in Scripture. In Leviticus, we learn how Israel was to distinguish between the clean and unclean. These categories extended to foods and animals. Even people could be defiled by disease or by touching unclean things such as a dead body. The temple was off-limits for the unclean. Only ritual washings and animal sacrifices made reentry into God’s presence achievable. But even this wasn’t permanent—for the blood of bulls and goats couldn’t fully atone for sin (Heb. 10:4). Like Israel, we dare not present ourselves before God in our sinful condition. As the psalmist asks, “Who shall stand in [God’s] holy place? He who has clean hands and a pure heart” (Ps. 24:3–4). While soap and water might wash our filthy hands, what can purify our sin-stained hearts? In today’s verses, the prophet Malachi announced the coming of One who would refine his people as gold and silver. Later, the author of Hebrews clarified the refiner’s identity: If the blood of goats and bulls . . . sanctify for the purification of the flesh, how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the eternal Spirit offered himself without blemish to God, purify our conscience from dead works to serve the living God. (Heb. 9:13–14) During Advent, we remember that Jesus is the great Refiner. He came to shed his purifying blood to cover our sins and forgive us. Then, like a refiner who heats metal to remove impurities, the Lord sanctifies us so that on judgment day we’ll be an unblemished offering to God. On that day, because of Jesus, we’ll wear white robes of righteousness (Rev. 6:11). Grandma made sure I looked pretty for church, but I wasn’t truly clean. Jesus, the great Purifier of sinners, is the only One who can wash away every stain and remove every impurity. When he dresses us in white robes, we’ll enter God’s presence because we’ll be clean—not just on the outside but on the inside too. Respond Sometimes the Lord refines us through trials and difficult circumstances. How have you experienced his refining process this year? Write a prayer thanking God for Christ who cleanses, purifies, and refines us so we’ll one day be holy and acceptable in his presence.

articles.title: Don’t Be Afraid of the Alien Question
articles.summary: ‘Faith in Space’ shows that many Americans throughout history have already taken the question of extraterrestrial life seriously, but they’ve done so from outside an orthodox Christian framework.
articles.summary_zh: ”“宇宙信仰”表明, 历史上许多美国人已经认真对待地球外生命问题,
articles.title_zh: 不要害怕外星人的问题
articles.content: Have you ever wondered whether other worlds exist, and, if they do, whether they’re filled with intelligent life? If so, you’ve tapped into a deeply human instinct. Americans have long looked up at the night sky and asked that question. For Christians, though, the answers can feel unnerving. We already believe in nonhuman intelligence. We call them angels and demons. But aliens would be something else—material, embodied, literally otherworldly . In 2016, NASA started a conversation among religious scholars at the Center of Theological Inquiry in Princeton about what the existence of extraterrestrial life would mean for religion. Paul Gutjahr, Ruth N. Halls professor of English at Indiana University, has been wrestling with that question for years. Faith in Space: American Religious Belief in Extraterrestrial Life is his considered answer. He thinks we need to look back at existing “extraterrestrial cosmologies” in American religions rather than merely pondering future possibilities (7). Faith in Space is ultimately a history of what happens when religious communities take extraterrestrial life seriously. Many minority religions have, and it has shaped their cosmology and even their soteriology. But for many evangelical Christians, Gutjahr’s history raises a more uncomfortable question: What happens when we don’t take seriously the possibility of extraterrestrial life? Alien Religion Early Americans didn’t need much help imagining inhabited worlds. According to Gutjahr, many Americans “believed there to be life elsewhere in the universe” (19). By the end of the 19th century, “every stratum of American society had been exposed” to this belief (43). For example, Emanuel Swedenborg taught that the universe is populated with humans bearing God’s image and claimed to have conversed with them. His American followers never numbered more than a few thousand, and yet his ideas traveled across the young nation; Helen Keller held them, as did John Chapman (a.k.a. Johnny Appleseed). What happens when we don’t take seriously the possibility of extraterrestrial life? Andrew Jackson Davis, the father of American Spiritualism, was similarly inspired, convinced that “if life is to be found on other planets, it is human life.” He arranged extraterrestrial humans in “a progression of degrees that move from less to more spiritual” (64). Then Joseph Smith took things further. Latter-day Saints (Mormons) took an “aggressive extraterrestrial cosmological stance,” linking all worlds under one governing structure (79). God created many inhabited worlds arranged in “a hierarchy where some worlds rule over others” (89). Among these many worlds, Earth holds the least desirable title of “the most wicked, and thus most in need of a savior” (86). God himself is an enfleshed exalted man dwelling on a planet near the star Kolob. I’d add that the Salt Lake Temple bears the Big Dipper, and early Latter-day Saint temple iconography is thick with suns, moons, and stars. Next came the founder of Seventh-day Adventism, Ellen G. White. Where William Miller’s followers read comets and meteor showers as signs of Christ’s return, White gave Seventh-day Adventists “a far more complex understanding of their relationship with the stars” (124). Ours “was the only wicked world” (125). White distinguished strongly between the righteous and unrighteous worlds, and put Earth on the wrong side of that distinction. By the 20th century, the heavens were packed and theories about the heavens were part of salvation. Then comes Helena Blavatsky (Theosophy), L. Ron Hubbard (Scientology), Wallace Fard Muhammad and Louis Farrakhan (Nation of Islam), Malachi Z. York (Nuwaubian Nation), Ashtar Command, and Heaven’s Gate. All these figures or groups saw extraterrestrial life as part of the human story, whether for our good or our ill, or both. 你有没有想过其他世界是否存在,如果存在,他们是否充满了智慧生命? 如果是这样的话,你已经深入到了人类的本能之中。 美国人早就仰望着夜空,问了这个问题. 但对于基督徒来说 答案会让人不安 我们已经相信非人类智慧 我们称他们为天使和恶魔。

但外星人会是别的东西——物质的,体现的,其实是异世界的。 2016年,NASA在普林斯顿神学调查中心开始了宗教学者之间的对话,讨论外星生命的存在对宗教的意义. 保罗·古特贾赫(Paul Gutjahr, Ruth N. Halls),印第安纳大学英语教授,多年来一直在与这个问题搏斗.

信仰太空:美国宗教信仰外星生活是他深思熟虑的答案. 他认为,我们需要回顾美国宗教中现有的“地外宇宙论”,而不是仅仅考虑未来的可能性(7)。 对太空的信仰最终是宗教界严肃对待外星生活时所发生的历史.

许多少数宗教都有,它塑造了他们的宇宙学甚至其神学. 但对于许多福音派基督徒来说, 如果我们不认真对待外星生命的可能性, 早期美国人不需要多少帮助,

Gutjahr说,许多美国人“相信宇宙中别处有生命”(19)。 到19世纪末,“美国社会的每一个阶层都暴露在”这种信念之下(43)。 例如,伊曼纽尔·瑞典堡教导说,宇宙中充满着带有上帝形象的人类,并声称与他们进行了交谈。

他的美国追随者人数从未超过几千人,然而他的想法却横跨了年轻的国家;海伦·凯勒也抱着他们,约翰·查普曼(英语:Johnny Appleseed)也是如此. 如果我们不认真对待外星生命的可能性,

美国精神主义之父安德鲁·杰克逊·戴维斯(Andrew Jackson Davis)同样受到启发,他坚信“如果在其他星球上找到生命,那就是人的生命。” 他将外星人类安排在“从较少的学位发展到更精神的学位”(64)。 后来约瑟夫·史密斯把事情更进一步.

末日圣徒(摩门教徒)采取了一种“侵略性的地外宇宙学立场,将所有的世界在一个管理结构下联系起来(79)。 上帝创造了许多有人居住的世界,这些世界是以“一些世界统治其他世界的等级”安排的(89)。 在许多世界中,地球拥有最不可取的“最邪恶因而最需要救世主”的称号(86)。

上帝本身就是一个被包围的尊贵的人, 住在一个靠近恒星科洛布的星球上。 盐湖寺内有大迪珀, 接下来是基督复临安息日会的创始人爱伦·G·怀特.

威廉·米勒的追随者将彗星和流星雨读作基督回归的标志,怀特给了基督复临安息日会信徒"对其与恒星关系的更复杂的理解"(124). 我们的“是唯一邪恶的世界”(125年)。 怀特强烈区分了正直和不公的世界,将地球置于这种区分的错误一边.

到了20世纪,诸天被收拾,关于诸天的理论是救赎的一部分. 接下来是Helena Blavatsky(Theosophy)、L. Ron Hubbard(科学学)、Wallace Fard Muhammad和Louis Farrakhan(伊斯兰联盟)、Malachi Z. York(努瓦乌比亚民族)、Ashtar指挥部和天门。

所有这些人物或团体将外星生命视为人类故事的一部分,无论是为了我们的好,还是为了我们的病,还是两者兼而有之. 虽然字幕承诺广泛覆盖美国宗教,但古特贾赫却抛弃了天主教徒,犹太人和本土传统. 唯一的“抗议者”h

articles.title: ‘I Was a Child of War’: How to Help Abuse Survivors Understand the Past
articles.summary: Yes, we were weak, but we were warriors, not victims.
articles.summary_zh: 是的，我们很弱小，但我们是战士，不是受害者。
articles.title_zh: “我曾是战争的孩子”：如何帮助虐待幸存者理解过去
articles.content: I grew up in a violent home, and it took me decades to find terms and categories that finally let me understand that aspect of my childhood. My first conversation partners and readings said I was a victim of abuse, but that framing was too passive to resonate with me. I believe the passive voice is valid, even essential. But when I discovered another framework, the child of war, I finally began to understand my past. Personal History That Led to Thoughts of War My father was a gifted professional, a compelling speaker who also possessed a shrewd wisdom. My mother seemed like a match—gifted, educated, and kind. But he was violent, even though for 16 years he was a pastor, and my mother couldn’t contain him. His behavior was our family secret, and if I hoped to understand it, I was on my own. Eventually, I read stories about one-dimensional moral monsters called “abusers”; their children were “victims.” But my parents seemed too admirable to be monsters, and the idea that I was a passive victim didn’t label my experience. I left home at 16 and essentially forgot the past until the month my father died. At that point, my readings on war let me see that my childhood had much in common with people who tried to resist and endure the aggression of a superior power. Terms like “resistance,” “war,” and “agency” fit better. They fostered understanding and healing. My first sharp memory is as ragged as a torn fingernail. Four years old, I’m hiding in my mother’s closet, behind dresses that smell of dust and skin cream. My skin stings and a deep ache runs beneath the surface. I’ve been spanked enough to know how it feels, but this is different. I think, I did something wrong, but what? I must deserve this, but why did he hit me so hard? Why does it hurt . . . so . . . much? I’m baffled by what we call mistreatment and betrayal. Fifty years later, I realized that 4-year-olds shouldn’t have the ability or experience to reflect critically on their beatings. And yet, because I could judge his actions, I could separate myself from him—he was “the” father rather than “my” father—and that gave me agency. When I turned 7, my favorite birthday gift was a miniature cowboy wagon. It was cheap, and the father quickly detected a flaw in the plastic. “This will snap,” he declared. He tugged and pulled at it until it broke, then he handed me the pieces and said, “See, I told you that would happen.” The playground had taught me that this was cruelty, so I decided to feel nothing , to sever his capacity to wound me. It was a foolish vow, one no child can fully keep, but it gave me a sense of agency or control. Two years later, it paid off. The chief gift for my 9th birthday was a basketball. When he decided I liked it too much, he stabbed it with a long knife. But by then, I’d hardened myself enough (agency again) to feel no grief, no surprise. It registered as a problem: Where would I get the money to buy another ball? How would I keep it safe? Because I could judge my father’s actions, I could separate myself from him, and that gave me agency. As time passed, my older brother and I began to resist him. We wore thick jeans when it seemed a belt might begin to fly. If a blow landed? Physical pain usually doesn’t last long. Social pains were tougher. The family moved often, because the father could always get a job but was too erratic to keep one. I attended five schools in seven years, chiefly in insular towns. I discovered that my athletic skills let me make friends through one team or another. Yet it was wise to mask my academic abilities-—unless the boys needed a math champion to wipe the smirks off the smart girls’ faces. I was making a way, until the dynamics at home shifted. Perhaps it was the alcohol. Perhaps it was the professional failure. The father was now reduced to the oversight of a tiny country church, two part-time jobs, and summer work for the Red Cross. Whatever the reasons, his behavior became ominous. He cursed and raged day after day,

我在一个暴力的家庭里长大,我花了几十年的时间才找到最终让我理解我童年的这一方面的术语和类别. 我的第一个谈话伙伴和读者说,我是虐待的受害者,但这种陷害太被动,无法与我产生共鸣。 我认为被动的声音是有效的,甚至是必不可少的。

但当我发现另一个框架,战争的孩子, 我终于开始理解我的过去。 个人历史 我父亲是一位有天赋的专业人士,一位很有说服力的演讲者,他拥有精明的智慧。 我妈妈看起来是一对配对, 虽然他16年来都是牧师,

他的行为是我们家族的秘密, 如果我希望理解它,我独自一人。 最终,我读到了关于一维道德怪物的故事,称为“滥用者 ” ; 他们的孩子是“受害者 ” 。 但我的父母似乎太令人钦佩了,

我16岁离开家 基本上忘记了过去 直到我父亲去世的那个月 那时,我对战争的解读让我看到,我的童年与那些试图抵抗和忍受一个超级大国的侵略的人们有许多共同点。 " 抵抗 " 、 " 战争 " 和 " 机构 " 等用语比较合适。 它们促进了理解和愈合。 我的第一个尖锐的记忆就像一个撕裂的手指甲一样

我躲在母亲的衣柜里, 我的皮肤刺痛 和深深的痛 运行在地表之下。 但情况不同。 我想,我做错了什么? 我必须得这样 但他为什么打我这么重? 为什么这么痛?

我对所谓的虐待和背叛感到困惑。 50年后,我意识到4岁的孩子不应该有批判性地反思殴打他们的能力或经验。 然而,因为我可以判断他的行为,我可以把自己与他分开——他是“父亲”而不是“我的父亲”,这给了我代理权。

当我七岁的时候 我最喜欢的生日礼物是一辆小型牛仔车 它很便宜,父亲很快发现了塑料的缺陷. 他宣称,“这将崩溃”。

他拉着它,拉着它,直到它破碎,然后他把碎片递给我,他说:你看,我告诉你了。 游乐场告诉我,这是残酷的, 所以我决定没有任何感觉, 切断他伤害我的能力。 这是一个愚蠢的誓言,一个没有孩子能完全保持的,但它给了我一种代理感或控制感. 两年之后,它得到了回报。

我九岁生日的主要礼物是篮球 当他决定我太喜欢它时 他用长刀刺它 但到那时,我已使自己变得足够坚固(又是一个机构),不感到悲伤,也不感到惊讶。 它是一个问题: 我哪来的钱买另一球? 我怎么保证它的安全?

因为我可以判断我父亲的行为, 随着时间流逝,我和哥哥开始反抗他. 我们穿着厚厚的牛仔裤 当它看起来可能开始飞翔。 如果一击落地? 身体疼痛通常不会持续很长时间。 社会痛苦更严重。

家里人经常搬家,因为父亲总是可以找到工作,但是过于不稳定,无法保留工作。 我在七年中就读了五所学校,主要在岛屿城镇。 我发现我的运动能力 让我通过一个或另一个团队交朋友。 除非男生需要数学冠军来抹去聪明女孩脸上的笑容,

我在想办法 直到家里的动态变化 也许是因为酒 也许是职业上的失败 父亲现在被降格为一个小乡村教会的监督,两个兼职工作,以及红十字会的暑期工作. 不管是什么原因 他的行为变得不祥 他日复一日的诅咒和愤怒,

articles.title_zh: 讲道中的陷阱：一封关于申请的信
articles.content: The following letter was published in the December 2025 issue of the Banner Magazine. It is published here at the request of a reader who found it helpful, in the hope that its counsel might be blessed to others also. You can also listen to a reading of this letter on the Banner Podcast. Dear J______, Following our conversation about application in preaching, I thought I would send along some thoughts I have had over the years on the subject. I want to point out some pitfalls you may want to keep in mind as you train R______. The only reason I know about them is from spending too much time in them myself! There has been a lot of self–examination and repenting over the years for me in this matter. The first thought is that too often (even in some of the best books on preaching) we hear that the text drives the sermon. This is a half-truth. A potentially dangerous half-truth. I have seen a man so intent on expositing his text well (and he did it very well) that he did not seem to notice or care that a third of the people in the room walked out before he finished preaching because he went on so long and the last meal of the conference was being served to meet the constraint of local train times. A wrong type of focus on the text and its explanation can make us oblivious to the very people the text is for. A preacher who stands up to preach having spent ninety per cent of his sermon preparation time in the week concentrating on the biblical text has not sufficiently realized what preaching actually is. In their book Letters Along the Way D. A. Carson and John Woodbridge put it this way: A chief reason why so much of what passes for evangelical expository preaching is so boring and irrelevant is that the preacher has spent a vastly disproportionate amount of preparation time in exegesis and outlines, and so little in thinking through how the Word of God is to wound and heal (to use the language of Hosea). 1 So preaching is about people. Preaching is about what God has to say to people about their lives . The text for a sermon is what God has to say to people . So the text of a sermon is like the recipe for a dish. A good cook would never be so focused on a recipe that she did not stop to realize that this was not at all the type of food her guests would need or appreciate. She would have her guests in mind from the start. After all, the goal of a good cook is not simply a matter of a recipe or a certain dish. It is feeding and feasting people . People drive the sermon. People are the reason God has given us the message in the biblical text. The biblical text leads the preacher to what the people need to hear from God. But the biblical text is only a means . The goal is people—to bring them somewhere that God wants them to go. To enlighten them, change them, help them, console them, correct them, train them to worship and serve God. People-oriented preaching comes from a God-centred, loving interest in them . Text-oriented preaching may simply come from the preacher’s love for preaching, for exegesis or for theology. A physician may be fascinated by medical treatments. But the good physician’s real interest is not treatments but people whose suffering has called for those treatments. Just so, true preaching is about people. That brings me to a second, related thought. We are often told that in preparing a sermon the key is finding the main idea of the text. To consider this as the key is not a people-oriented point of view and does not produce good preaching. It produces preaching with lots of emphasis on ideas and little emphasis on application. The key to preparing a sermon is not to find the main idea of the text. It is to find the main goal of the text. Not ‘What does the biblical text mainly say?’ But rather ‘What does this text intend to mainly do for people?’ What does the text intend mainly to effect in the lives of people? What does this text aim to move the people to believe, to do, to become? Application! A. T. Pierson, i
articles.content_zh: 以下信件发表于"班纳杂志"2025年12月号. 它应一位读者的要求在这里出版,他觉得它很有帮助,希望它的律师也能得到他人的祝福。 也可以在"班纳·波德克特"上收听对这封信的读取. 亲爱的J-,在我们讨论申请布道后,我想,我将提出一些多年来我对这一问题的看法。 我想指出一些陷阱 你可能想记住 当你训练R. 我了解他们的唯一原因 就是自己花太多时间在他们身上 多年来,我一直以来都在自责自悔。 第一种想法是,太多时候(即使在一些关于布道的好书中),我们听到文字驱动布道. 这是半个事实。 一个潜在的危险 半真相。 我见过一个男人如此有意地公开他的文字(他做得非常好),他似乎没有注意到或关心房间里有三分之一的人在他完成布道之前就离开,因为他走了这么长一段时间,会议的最后一餐是用来应付当地火车时间的限制。 错误地注重案文及其解释会使我们忘记案文所要为的人。 一位挺身而出进行传道的传道者,在一周里,他90%的布道准备时间都集中在圣经文本上,但是他没有充分意识到实际的传道内容。 在他们所著的"沿着路"(Letrys A. A. Carson)和"约翰·伍德布里奇"(John Woodbridge)一书中这样写道: 传福音的宣讲之所以如此之多,实在是无趣而无关紧要的一个主要原因是,传道人花费了大量的不相称的准备时间来解剖和提纲,在思考"上帝之道"是怎样去伤口和愈合(使用"霍西"的语言)时却很少考虑. 1个 故传道以人为事. 意义在于上帝要对人们说 他们的生活 讲道的文字是上帝要对人们说的话。 所以布道的文字就像菜谱。 一个好厨师永远也不会把注意力集中在一个配方上,以至于她不禁意识到这根本不是客人需要或欣赏的食物类型. 她一开始就想着她的客人 毕竟,一个好厨师的目标不仅仅是一个菜谱或某种菜肴的问题. 它在给人们提供食物和盛宴。 人们驱使布道。 人们是上帝给我们圣经文本中的信息的原因。 圣经文本将传道人引向人们需要从上帝那里听到的. 但圣经文本只是一个手段。 目标是人们,把他们带到上帝要他们去的地方去。 为了启蒙他们,改变他们,帮助他们,安慰他们,矫正他们,训练他们去崇拜并服务于上帝. 以人为中心的布道来自以上帝为中心, 以文字为取向的传道可能只是来自传道者对传道、开教或神学的热爱。 医生可能因治疗而着迷。 但好医生的真正兴趣不是治疗,而是那些遭受痛苦需要治疗的人。 所以,真正的传道是关于人的。 这让我想到另一个相关的想法。 我们经常被告知,在准备布道时,关键在于找到案文的主要想法。 将此视为关键不是以人民为导向的观点,也不产生好传道. 它产生许多强调思想的布道,很少强调应用。 准备布道的关键不是找到文本的主要想法. 它是为了找到案文的主要目标。 而非"圣经主要说些什么?" 但更确切地说,“这个文本主要是为了什么?” 案文主要打算如何影响人们的生活? 这个文字的目的是要促使人们相信,去做,变成什么? 申请! A. T. 皮尔逊,i

articles.summary_zh: 我们都需要对上帝对所有众生和事件的主权统治有更大的敏感性。亚历山大·卡森（ Alexander Carson ）的研究《圣经所体现的天意的历史》（ The History of Providence as Manifested in Scripture ）可以帮助我们培养这种敏感性。以下是耶利米书第14章中他对犹大饥荒主题的评论：由于饥荒的存在， […]犹大的饥荒后：上帝的普罗维登斯显示首先出现在美国真理的旗帜上。
articles.title_zh: 犹大饥荒：神的普罗维登斯显现
articles.content: We all need a greater sensitivity to God’s sovereign rule over all beings and events. Alexander Carson’s study, The History of Providence as Manifested in Scripture can help train us in such sensitivity. Here are his comments on the subject of famine in Judah from Jeremiah 14: FOR the existence of plenty as of famine, the wisdom of this world looks no higher than to what are called second causes. God, it is considered, is no farther concerned in these matters than as the author of certain general laws. He has set the machine a-going, and it continues to work by its own construction, without any regulation of a superintending hand. Climate, soil, cultivation, need, it is confessed, favourable seasons, but any divine direction of weather is supposed to be unnecessary. Timely rain—or the want of it, is a matter below the attention of the Ruler of the world. The blight and the mildew, the wet and the caterpillar, are enemies with which the farmer is to struggle; but they are never considered as armies of devastation sent into the fields by a righteous Providence. The history of the Old Testament gives us a key to Providence in the production of famine or of plenty. God regulates the supplies of the children of men as exactly as if each individual of the human race had his rations assigned him by the angels of heaven every rising sun: ‘The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning the dearth. Judah mourneth, and the gates thereof languish; they are black unto the ground; and the cry of Jerusalem is gone up. And their nobles have sent their little ones to the waters: they came to the pits, and found no water; they returned with their vessels empty: they were ashamed and confounded, and covered their heads. Because the ground is chapt, for there was no rain in the earth, the ploughmen were ashamed, they covered their heads. Yea, the hind also calved in the field, and forsook it, because there was no grass. And the wild asses did stand in the high places, they snuffed up the wind like dragons; their eyes did fail, because there was no grass. O Lord, though our iniquities testify against us, do thou it for thy name’s sake: for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against thee.’—Jer. 14:1–7. As in creation and in Providence, so in redemption, God hides himself in the midst of a blaze of light. In all his works he reveals himself, yet the enmity of the human heart will not allow men to see him. And what is most strange, the savage sees a divine hand in the works of Providence; it is unseen and denied by philosophical wisdom. The illiterate peasant hears God in his voice of thunder and storms, and acknowledges divine wrath in pestilence, sword, and famine. But the philosopher perceives nothing in all these but the course of nature. The wisdom of man makes itself ignorant of what the very beasts seem to feel. Read more: The History of Providence As Manifested in Scripture by Carson, Alexander price From: $ 13.50 Learn More Select Options Description A subject of the deepest interest to the Christian.’ Takes the reader through the Scriptures and points to instances of God’s providence which will provide comfort for all true believers. 264pp. Featured Photo (visible when the piece is shared on social media) is a detail from one by Oz Seyrek on Unsplash The post Famine in Judah: God’s Providence Displayed appeared first on Banner of Truth USA .
articles.content_zh: 我们都需要更加关注上帝对所有生命和事件的主权统治。 Alexander Carson的研究, 《普罗维登斯的历史》, 以下是他从耶利米14号对犹大饥荒主题的评论: 对于饥荒时存在的富足,这个世界的智慧看起来并不比所谓的"第二原因"更高. 据认为,与某些一般法律的制定者相比,上帝在这些事务上没有更多的关切。 他把机器设为正常运行,它继续按自己的构造运作,没有任何管制的上司手. 气候,土壤,种植,需要,是承认的,有利的季节,但是任何神圣的天气方向都应该是不必要的. 及时降雨——或者说,这是世界统治者不关心的问题。 荒凉和温和的、湿润的和毛毛的,是农民要与之斗争的敌人;但他们从未被视为正义的普罗维登斯派入田地的毁灭军队。 "旧约"的历史为我们提供了普罗维登斯产生饥荒或富饶的关键. 真主为世人的给养而加以管理,犹如每个人的给养,每逢太阳升起,就奉天天神所赐给每个人一样。 犹大哀悼而其中的城门枯萎;他们已变成黑色的;耶路撒冷的呼声已升起。 其贵人又将小人送入水中去:来入坑中去,又无取出水来;又以器物入空而回;自惭而自愧,自蒙而出. 因为地是分明的,因为地上没有下雨,犁地人感到羞愧,就把头盖了起来. 有之,后人又以地为牛,而弃之,因有草而去. 野驴们的确站在高处,他们像龙一样把风扑倒;他们的眼睛确实衰败了,因为没有草. 主啊!我们的罪过虽能证明我们的罪过,但求你为你的名字而行之;我们的背负是多的;我们确已犯罪了。 与创造和普罗维登斯一样,在救赎中,上帝将自己隐藏在一束光芒中. 在他的所有作品中,他都暴露了自己,然而人心的敌意却不允许人见到他. 最奇怪的是,野蛮人看到普罗维登斯的作品中有神之手;它是看不见的,被哲学智慧所否定. 文盲农民在雷和风暴中听到上帝的声音,在瘟疫、剑和饥荒中承认神圣的愤怒。 但是哲学家在所有这些事物中,除了自然的走向,什么也看不出来. 人类的智慧使自己对野兽的感受一无所知. 更多信息:卡森所著"普罗维登斯的历史"(The History of Providence As Expressed in Books by Carson, Alexander price from: $ 13.50 学习更多选择选项描述) 基督教徒最感兴趣的话题。 以天经为阅读者,并举出真主赐予信士们的慰藉。 264pp. Featured Photo(当作品在社交媒体上分享时可以看见),

articles.title_zh: 让苦涩的东西变甜的上帝
articles.content: The Israelites had just walked between the walls of the water of the Red Sea and watched as the Lord washed away the whole Egyptian army. They sang a song of triumph on the far shore of the sea, rejoicing in the fear that had fallen on the surrounding nations (Ex. 15:14-16) and looking forward to taking possession of the Promised Land in the near future (Ex. 15:17). But within three days they raised a very different kind of sound—a chorus of grumbling against Moses because there was no water to drink at Marah (Ex. 15:22-26). I wonder what they expected would happen after the Red Sea. A straight, unhindered journey to the land flowing with milk and honey? Instead the first thing the Lord does is to lead his people to the undrinkable water of Marah. There is no question that the Lord is the one who led them there—it is easy enough to take a wrong turn when you are following Google Maps, but not when you are following a towering pillar of cloud or fire! So why did God lead Israel to Marah? Is it because he is sadistic and cruel and takes delight in watching his people suffer dehydration and fear? Is it because he is really bad at geography? Of course not! In fact we’re told why he brought Israel to Marah in Ex. 15:25: There the Lord tested them. In fact, the whole wilderness is a place of testing. That’s the significance of the wilderness—it’s a hard place. Deuteronomy 8:15 calls it ‘the vast and dreadful wilderness, that thirsty and waterless land, with its venomous snakes and scorpions.’ God is training his infant son to trust him—and training is always painful. There are no short cuts, whether in the physical training of our bodies to make them stronger and faster, or in the mental training of our minds to increase our knowledge and understanding, or in the spiritual training of our souls to grow in godliness. Learning to trust God is not something we can do lounging on the sofa. It means being put into situations that are stressful, confusing, messy and complicated, when we don’t understand what is going on or see any answers. Anyone can trust God when things are easy; the real test is if you will trust God when things are tough. Israel’s failure Marah was Israel’s first test and they failed. They have been travelling for three days and haven’t found any water. Supplies are running low. Perhaps as they saw the waters of Marah in the distance they finished up their last reserves: ‘It’ll be OK—we can refill very soon!’ Imagine the relief and joy as the first to reach Marah fall down and scoop the water to their mouths. And imagine them spitting it out as they discover it is foul and undrinkable. They’re not just disappointed—they’re horrified . Panic seizes them. ‘What shall we drink?’ (v. 24) This is not like someone in a restaurant complaining that their steak is a bit on the tough side or that the soup is a tad cold. They are exhausted and dehydrated and they can’t see any way of getting water. Suddenly life is hanging by a thread. There is nothing unreasonable about their concern. That is not why they fail the test. They fail the test because of their attitude. They grumble: the word means ‘hostile complaining, verbal attacks of dissatisfied people.’ Why do they grumble? There are at least two reasons: Faithlessness . They do not trust God. They don’t trust his power (that he can take care of them) or his goodness (that he wants to take care of them). They should have gone to the Lord with their needs, humbly asking him to provide what they needed. And this lack of faith was due to… Forgetfulness . This is the diagnosis of Psalm 78:40ff: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness and grieved him in the desert! … They did not remember his power or the day when he redeemed them from the foe , 43 when he performed his signs in Egypt and his marvels in the fields of Zoan. The people had such short memories! It has only been three days since they walked through the Red Sea! It has been just a few weeks since they witn
articles.content_zh: 以色列人刚刚走入了红海的水墙之间,看着上帝冲走整个埃及军队。 他们在远海岸上唱了一首"胜利之歌",欣喜地感受到了降临于周边民族的恐惧(Ex. 15:14-16)并期待着在不久的将来占有所承诺之地(Ex. 15:17). 但他们在三日内,举出一种非常不同的声音,一种对穆萨抱怨的合唱,因为在马拉没有水可饮(前15:22-26). 不知道红海之后他们会怎样 直走无阻地去 充满牛奶和蜂蜜的土地? 取而代之的是,主所行之事,是引其民入于马拉所出不可饮之水也. 毫无疑问,主是带领他们到那里去的——当你遵循Google地图时,很容易错转,但当你遵循高耸起的云柱或火柱时,就不是了! 那么为什么上帝带领以色列找到马拉? 是不是因为他是虐待狂和残忍的,在看着他的人民遭受脱水和恐惧时感到愉快? 是不是因为他在地理上很不好? 当然不是! 事实上我们被告知他为何在前15:25将以色列带到马拉:上帝在那里测试过他们。 事实上,整个荒地都是试验地. 这是荒野的意义, 8: 15 脱胎手术称之为:"大而可怕的荒野, 渴而无水之地, 有毒蛇和蝎子. 真主正在训练他的儿子,以便他信任他。训练确是痛苦的。 无论是身体锻炼,使其更强而更快,还是心灵修炼,以增进我们的知识和理解,或是心灵修炼,以在教化中成长,都没有任何短短的削减. 学会相信上帝不是我们能在沙发上做的事 这表示当我们不明白发生了什么情况或看到答案时, 当事情变得容易的时候,任何人都可以信任真主;真正的考验是,如果事情变得艰难的时候,你们要信任真主的话。 以色列的失败马拉是以色列的第一个考验, 他们已经旅行了三天, 补给不足。 也许当他们看到马拉的海水, 想象一下,解脱和欢乐是第一个到达马拉的人倒下,把水灌入口中. 想象一下他们发现它肮脏而不可饮用时就吐出它. 他们不仅失望, 恐慌抓住他们。 我们喝什么? (v.24) 这不像餐馆里有人抱怨 他们的牛排有点硬 或者汤有点冷 他们已经精疲力竭并脱水, 突然间,生命被一丝一缕地挂起 他们的关切没有什么不合理的。 这并不是他们失败的原因。 他们因为态度而未能通过测试. 他们抱怨道:这个词的意思是“敌意抱怨, 他们为什么抱怨? 至少有两个原因:失信。 他们不相信上帝。 他们不相信他的能力(他能照顾他们)或善良(他想照顾他们), 他们应该带着自己的需要去主那里,谦卑地要求他提供他们需要的东西. 缺乏信心是因为... 这就是对"诗经"78:40ff的诊断:他们在荒野中频繁地反抗他,在沙漠中为他悲伤!...... 他们不记得他的威力,也不记得他从敌人手中赎回他们的那一天,43岁时他在埃及行过他的迹象,他在Zoan地上行过他的奇事。 人们记忆很短! 他们从红海走过才三天! 几周前他们才开始

articles.summary_zh: 六个帖子中的第四个帖子包含了阿尔伯特· N ·马丁（ Albert N. Martin ）在1984年旗帜青年大会（ Banner Youth Conference ）上给出的教学内容，展示了基督教生活的基本圣经神学。在基督徒的生活中，没有承诺或命令的危机经历是必不可少的元素。一些关于基督徒生活的教导断言， […]《基督徒生活中没有必要的危机经历》一文首先出现在《美国真理旗帜》上。
articles.title_zh: 在基督徒的生活中，没有必要的危机经历
articles.content: The fourth of six posts containing the substance of teaching given by Albert N. Martin at the 1984 Banner Youth Conference, presenting a basic biblical theology of the Christian life. There is no crisis experience promised or commanded as an essential element in living the Christian life. Some teaching on the Christian life asserts that only a low level of Christian experience can be realized by the person who has not had a crisis experience subsequent to regeneration, or at least subsequent to conversion and to the beginning of conscious Christian experience. Furthermore, it is asserted that the crisis experience is both commanded and promised by God as the entrance into a qualitatively new dimension or level of spiritual experience, reality and power. Throughout the history of the Christian church there have been many different strands of this crisis teaching. There is what we might call ‘classic Wesleyan perfectionism,’ which concentrated particularly upon sanctification and spoke of a baptism of purifying fire, or of coming into a state of perfect love. It concentrated not so much on power for service or upon inward feelings, but on a crisis experience in which the power of indwelling sin was to all intents and purposes negated. I have read enough of classic Wesleyan theology to know that there are different opinions as to what John Wesley himself taught on the subject. But in a general descriptive manner this, I believe, is an accurate representation of old-style classic Wesleyan perfectionism. Then, too, there is ‘the old Pentecostalism’ in which the emphasis was upon a baptism in the Holy Spirit, generally subsequent to conversion, and invariably manifested by speaking in tongues: the way you knew that you had this baptism of power was that, when it came to you, you spoke in tongues. The primary focus in old classic Pentecostalism was the matter of power for service. Thirdly, there is the modern ‘charismatic movement.’ Like classic Pentecostalism, its teachers use many of the same passages in the Book of Acts to support their theory of this necessary crisis. So they emphasize that in most cases—although there are different schools among modern charismatics—it will be manifested by the speaking in tongues. Some are content to believe you have ‘got it’ if you have a season of holy laughter. Others, however, say that you have not spoken in tongues because you have some psychological hold-ups, and if these can be removed the tongues are there. You just have not given them utterance. Here the emphasis is not so much on a baptism of purifying fire (as in the case of old classic Wesleyan perfectionism), or the baptism of power (as in the case of old classic Pentecostalism), but more upon a baptism of joyful praise-filled experience. I have been speaking of generalities, but I believe they are accurate. Fourthly, there are the various forms of ‘higher life’ teaching. What they have in common is this: you are simply converted, simply united to Christ, simply regenerated, and then you come to a crisis of surrender and faith, in which ‘you let go and let God’ and appropriate the indwelling life of Christ. The common denominator is that it is a crisis without any external manifestation of tongues or holy laughter or shouting or jumping, but the end result will be new power to live a holy life—the emphasis falls upon the ability to be more efficient in the path of holiness. Fifthly, there is a kind of teaching which has both old and modern proponents. It focuses on assurance, and has been expressed in terms of the biblical language of a ‘sealing of the Holy Spirit.’ Some of the Puritans—Thomas Goodwin, for example—taught this. There have been certain preachers in our own day who have believed this very strongly and emphasized it repeatedly. The basic concern in this teaching is that, subsequent to regeneration and conversion, there is a crisis experience in which the believer enters into a qualitatively new dimension of assurance by
articles.content_zh: 阿尔伯特·N·马丁在1984年班纳青年会议上发表的包含教学内容的六篇文章中的第四篇,介绍了基督教生活的基本圣经神学. 没有任何危机经历作为过上基督教生活的一项基本要素得到承诺或接受。 一些关于基督教生活的教义主张,在再生后,或至少是在皈依后,以及自觉的基督教经历开始后,没有危机经历的人,只有低水平的基督教经验才能实现. 此外,有人断言,危机经历既是上帝的旨意,也是上帝的允诺,是精神经历、现实和力量进入一个全新的层面或层次的。 在基督教会的历史上,这种危机教育有许多不同的内容。 我们可能称之为“经典的卫斯理完美主义 ” , 它不是把精力集中在服务或内在感情上,而是集中在一种危机经历上,在这种经历中,罪恶的威力是所有意图和目的所否定的。 我读了足够多的经典的卫斯理神学,知道对于约翰·卫斯理自己教授的这个主题,有不同的看法. 但从一般的描述方式来看,我认为,这是对老式经典的卫斯理主义的准确表述. 也存在“五旬节派”的旧现象, 重点是圣灵中的洗礼, 通常是在皈依之后, 古老的经典五旬节主义的主要焦点是服务的权力问题. 第三,有现代`魅力运动'。 和经典的五旬节主义一样,它的老师们也用"行动书"中的许多同名段落来支持他们对这个必要危机的理论. 所以他们强调,在多数情况下,尽管现代魅力中存在着不同的学校,但用舌头说话将表明这一点。 如果你有一个圣笑的季节, 然而,其他人说,你没有说出舌头,因为你有一些心理障碍,如果这些障碍可以取出,舌头就在那里。 你只是没说 这里强调的不是净化火的洗礼(如旧经典的卫斯理完美主义),也不是权力的洗礼(如旧经典的五旬节主义),而是更强调充满欢乐的赞美经验的洗礼. 我一直在谈论泛泛而谈,但我认为它们是正确的。 第四,有各种形式的 " 更高的生活 " 教学。 他们的共同点是:你们只是皈依正教,只是与基督联合,只是再生,然后你们遭遇了投降和信仰的危机,你们在危机中“放手,放任真主出征”,而顺从基督永生。 共同的分母是,这是一场没有外在表现出舌头或圣笑或叫喊或跳跃的危机,但最终结果将是新的力量来过上圣生活——强调在圣道上更有效率的能力. 第五,有一种教学既有老的也有现代的支持者。 它侧重于保证,并用圣经中的"封圣"来表述. 一些清教徒——例如托马斯·古德温——教授了这个。 在我们这一天里,有一些传道者非常强烈地相信并反复强调这一点。 该教学的基本关注是,在再生和转生之后,存在着一种危机经历,信仰者通过下列方式进入了保证的质的新层面:

articles.title: Spoiled for Choice: Two New Graphic Novels of Pilgrim’s Progress
articles.summary: Two new graphic novel adaptations of Pilgrim’s Progress have arrived within weeks of each other. Here's how they are similar and different, and my recommendation of which one to buy. See Also A La Carte (July 27) The Puritans: John Bunyan A La Carte (6/3)
articles.summary_zh: 两部《天路历程》的全新漫画改编作品在相隔数周的时间内相继面世。以下是它们的异同之处，以及我对于购买哪一本的建议。另见《A La Carte》（7月27日）《清教徒：约翰·班扬》《A La Carte》（6月3日）
articles.title_zh: 选择多多：两部全新《天路历程》绘本小说
articles.content: I have often expressed how spoiled Christian readers are today. As if we needed more proof of this, how about the fact that in a single month, publishers released not one but two major graphic novel adaptations of Pilgrim’s Progress ? Both are well-written, beautifully illustrated, and faithful to Bunyan’s story. Let me help you understand their similarities and differences and tell you which one might be best to add to your library. Christian’s Quest is written by Tyler Van Halteren and illustrated by Manuel Zepic. It is published by Lithos Kids, which has already released the three-part Little Pilgrim’s Big Journey , an illustrated adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress for young readers, and The Mansoul Chronicles , which is based on Bunyan’s Holy War . It is a 220-page 7×10.63 inch hardcover that targets children aged 8+, though it is meant to be enjoyed by teens and adults as well. Its illustrations are what I might describe as a clean, polished YA style. The lines are thin and tidy and much of the form comes from shading. The colors tend to maintain a soft, muted, painted look. It lightly updates some antiquated language so that Bunyan’s Slough of Despond becomes the Bog of Despond. Christian is youthful and fresh-faced, and his burden is a bulging pack on a frame. It includes some bonus material: a behind-the-scenes look at how a graphic novel is made, and a study guide that explains and applies each of the stages of Christian’s quest. It also indicates that a sequel, Christiana’s Crown , will be released in 2028. Pilgrim’s Progress: The Graphic Novel is written by Jeremy Patenaude, illustrated by Brent McKee, colored by Matt Wilson, and lettered by Taylor Esposito. It is published by Crossway as what I believe is the company’s first graphic novel, though it has a long history of publishing books for young readers. It is a 256-page 7×10.25 inch paperback that targets readers aged 14+. Its illustrations are what I might describe as gritty and stylized and perhaps a bit more indie than mainstream. It uses heavy brush ink, dark shadows, and vivid colors. It does not update Bunyan’s antiquated language. Christian is a gaunt, tormented, weathered adult whose burden is a huge stone roped to his back. Its bonus material includes a lexicon of the key characters and locations and reflections on each of the chapters. There is no indication of a sequel that will cover Christiana’s quest. While these two graphic novels tell the same story and tell it faithfully using dialogue and illustration rather than narration, they tell it using different visual language largely because Christian’s Quest is meant to be accessible to a younger demographic. You might say that Christian’s Quest is a bit more kid-friendly and Pilgrim’s Progress is a bit more adult-friendly, though both could easily be enjoyed by kids and adults alike. After all, who doesn’t enjoy reading the occasional graphic novel? Another key difference is that Pilgrim’s Progress is a paperback where Christian’s Quest is being sold as more of an heirloom object that features cloth binding, gold foil, and a ribbon marker. Let me show you a few examples of the art from each book. Christian’s Quest These are drawn from the publisher’s preview images. Pilgrim’s Progress These are drawn from the sample chapter on Crossway’s site. My Recommendation Which do I recommend? Either! Both! If your readers are younger, Christian’s Quest is the more obvious choice, and if they are older—teenagers and up—they may prefer Pilgrim’s Progress . But you couldn’t go wrong with either, and you couldn’t go wrong with picking up both. Where to Buy Christian’s Quest Lithos Kids · clothbound hardcover · ages 8+ Buy at Amazon Westminster Books Pilgrim’s Progress: The Graphic Novel Crossway · paperback · ages 14+ Buy at Amazon Westminster Books See Also A La Carte (July 27) The Puritans: John Bunyan A La Carte (6/3)
articles.content_zh:
我经常表达基督教读者今天是多么的被宠坏。 似乎我们需要更多的证据, 在一个月里, 出版商只发行了两部关于朝圣者进步的重要小说改编。 他们都写得很好,

让我来帮助你理解它们之间的相似之处和差异,并告诉你,哪一个可能最好加入你的图书馆. 由泰勒·范·哈特伦(英语:Tyler Van Halteren)撰写,曼努埃尔·泽皮奇(英语:Manuel Zepic)作画.

由Lithos Kids出版, 已经发行了三部曲小朝圣者大旅, 这是一项220页的7x10.63英寸硬盖,针对的是8岁以上儿童,但青少年和成年人也享受。

它的插图是我可以描述的 一种干净,光泽的YA风格。 线条细而整齐,形式大多来自阴影. 颜色倾向于保持柔软,沉默,绘画的外观. 它轻而易举地更新了一些古老的语言,使邦扬的"Despond的Slough"成为了Despond的Bog. 克里斯蒂安年轻又新面孔,他的担子是架子上的膨胀包.

包括一些奖品:一幅幕后小说是如何制作的,一幅研究指南解释并应用了基督教的追求的每个阶段。 这部续集《克里斯蒂安娜的王冠》将于2028年发行。

朝圣者的进步:图画小说由Jeremy Patenaude写作,布伦特·麦基(Brent Mckee)饰演,马特·威尔逊饰演,泰勒·埃斯波西托(Taylor Esposito)饰演. 由Crossway出版, 我认为这是公司的第一部平面小说, 它有256页7x10.25英寸的纸质背面,针对14岁以上读者。

它的插图是我可以说的 粗糙和结构化, 可能比主流多一点。 它使用重笔墨,暗影,以及生动的色彩. 它不会更新Bunyan的过时语言。 克里斯蒂安是一个胆小, 受折磨,风化的成年人, 他的负担是一个巨大的石头绑在背上。

它的奖金材料包括关键人物和地点的词汇表以及对每一章的思考. 没有迹象表明会续集克里斯蒂安娜的追求。

虽然这两部图画小说讲述了同一个故事,忠实地用对话和插图来讲述,而不是用不同的视觉语言讲述,这主要是因为克里斯蒂安的Quest本意是让年轻人口能够接触到.

基督教徒的追问更适合孩子, 朝圣者的进步更适合成年人, 毕竟,谁不喜欢偶尔读那本图画小说?

另一个关键区别是,朝圣者的进步是一个纸质的回扣,在那里,基督教的Quest被作为更多的继承物出售,该物的特点是布装、金瓦和丝带标志。 让我给你们看看每本书中的一些艺术例子。 基督教的追问 这些照片来自出版商的预览图像。

朝圣者的进步 照片来自Crossway网站的样本章节。 我的建议 我推荐哪个? 也没有! 都一样! 如果你的读者年轻,基督教的“追问”是更明显的选择,如果他们是年长的年轻人,他们可能更喜欢朝圣者的进步。 但你也不可能出错,

8岁+在亚马逊威斯敏斯特书店买书:图画小说十字路口 页面存档备份,存于互联网档案馆 14岁+在亚马逊威斯敏斯特书店买书

articles.title: Scrolling the Soul Shallow
articles.summary: Entertainment swamps nearly all of life in triviality. So, how can we resist the tide and embrace a wholehearted, soul-satisfying pursuit of God? Listen Now
articles.summary_zh: 娱乐将生活的几乎所有方面都淹没在琐碎之中。那么，我们该如何抵挡这股潮流，全心全意地追求神，让灵魂得到满足呢？马上收听
articles.title_zh: 滚动灵魂浅滩
articles.content: Audio Transcript We lived through a decade of smartphone abuse and overuse (roughly 2015 to 2024). We talked at length about it on this podcast. I wrote books about it. Most of us have come to terms with when and where we’ve been online too much. We lament the wasted time, knowing we should have been doing more important things. The clock sped up as we lost ourselves in the everlasting scroll of eye-grabbing images and video. But what if time was not the greatest cost? What if something more serious happened to us, a lingering damage still present inside of us now? Today on Ask Pastor John: scrolling the soul shallow. It’s a question from Noah, a young man in Akron, Ohio. “Pastor John, I have made Titus 2:6–8 my aim as a young man. I know Paul is speaking to a young pastor. I am not a pastor, but I want to be self-controlled. I want to show myself ‘to be a model of good works,’ and I want to display ‘integrity, dignity, and sound speech.’ The main struggle I face is the shallowness of the culture in which we live. On my phone, computer, and TV, I see endless examples of flippancy. That’s really all I see some days. The whole world seems bent on numbing our souls to eternal realities. How can a young man resist all this and stay spiritually alert and cultivate these virtues?” One of the reasons I love this question is because I have said many times that the worst problem with television (or now let’s just say Instagram or any online media in general) is probably not the pervasive sexualization of all of life — that’s big enough — but rather the pervasive trivialization of all of life. You can scarcely watch TV ads or be online for more than ten seconds without being dump-trucked with banality and silliness. Grown men and women, even famous grown men and women, act like eleven-year-olds whose high point at summer camp was to bob for apples in a toilet filled with Mello Yello — the apex of satisfaction. That’s the quality that we’re being dumped on every day. This is the world we live in: silliness, humor, fun, joking, casual, flippant, cleverness, whimsical. And all that has made its way tragically into parenting, worship services, preaching, and hosting an event, even a serious one. Many modern people have never tasted serious joy, glad gravity, happy earnestness, or joyful weightiness. They have no category for such a thing. There’s fun and there’s boredom. That’s it. Life is that shallow, that insignificant. So, Noah asks, “How can I resist all this? How can I march to the beat of a different drummer?” 1. Distinguish between joy and fun. First, make sure that you are clear that joy and fun are not identical. Today, the word fun has virtually taken over the experience of serious joy. “Think about the shortness of life and the inevitability of death and the great realities of God.” Fun is what you have when playing with your kids on the living-room floor, flag football with the guys on Saturday, or a day at Disney World. That’s fun — nothing wrong with it. But now, church planting is fun, worship services are fun, Bible studies are fun. It’s as if you learn the language of trees while walking among twenty-foot Georgia pines, and then you visit three-hundred-foot, two-thousand-year-old redwoods in California and you have no language. They’re just fun trees. They’re not magnificent. They’re not breathtaking. They’re not humbling. They’re just fun trees. So, Noah, grow your vocabulary of joy and significance and wonder, because more often than we would like to admit, the heart shrinks to the language we have to express it rather than the other way around. If you call enough magnificent things “fun,” before long, that’s all they’ll be. Your heart will have shrunk to your vocabulary. 2. Know you’re not crazy. Second, listen to the warnings of Scripture to know you’re not crazy. The Bible is very aware of people who are incapable of being happily serious, and all their language is just clever or joking or trifling. - “Like a madman w

音频记录 我们经历了十年的智能手机虐待和过度使用(大约2015年到2024年). 我们在播客上详细谈论了这个问题。 我写过书 我们大部分人都同意我们上网的时间和地点。 我们对浪费时间感到遗憾,因为我们知道我们应该做更重要的事。

时钟加速了,因为我们迷失了自己 在永恒的卷轴 挖眼影像和视频。 但如果时间不是最大的代价呢? 如果更严重的事情发生在我们身上, 那现在我们体内仍然存在的伤害呢? 今天在"问约翰牧师"上:滚动灵魂浅浅. 俄亥俄州Akron的年轻人Noah问:

“约翰神父,我把提图斯2:6-8作为我作为年轻人的目标。 我知道保罗在和一个年轻的牧师说话 我不是牧师,但我想自我控制。 我想展示自己“成为优秀作品的典范”, 我面临的主要斗争是我们所生活的文化的浅浅.

在我的手机、电脑和电视上, 我看到无尽的翻转例子。 这些日子我只看到这些。 整个世界似乎都想把我们的灵魂麻木于永恒的现实。

一个年轻人怎么能抗拒这一切,保持精神警惕,培养这些美德呢?” 我喜欢这个问题的原因之一 是因为我已经说过很多次了 电视最糟糕的问题(或者现在我们只说Instagram或任何一般的网络媒体) 可能不是 普遍的性化 生活的所有 - 这已经够大了 - 而是 普遍的轻视所有o

f 寿. 你几乎不能看电视广告 或在线超过十秒 而不被垃圾车 与平庸和愚蠢。 长大的男女,甚至著名的成年男女,都表现得像11岁的孩子,他们在夏令营的高潮是在充满了梅洛·耶洛的厕所里为苹果吹嘘——满足的顶峰. 这就是我们每天被抛弃的质量。

这就是我们生活的世界: 愚蠢、幽默、有趣、开玩笑、随意、放荡、聪明、狂喜。 在养育子女、礼拜、传教和主持活动,甚至是严肃的活动方面,所有这一切都是可悲的。 许多现代人从未品尝过严肃的喜悦,快乐的引力,快乐的真诚,或者欢乐的重量. 他们没有这样的分类。

有乐趣和无聊。 就这样。 生命是那么浅,那么微不足道。 诺亚问道:我怎能抗拒这一切呢? 我怎能走向一个不同的鼓手呢?” 1.区分欢喜乐. 第一,确保你明白快乐和乐趣并不相同。 今天,乐趣一词几乎取代了严肃的欢乐经历.

“考虑到生命的短暂性、死亡的必然性和上帝的伟大现实。” 有趣的是,当你在客厅地板上和孩子们玩时, 星期六和男生一起打橄榄球, 或者一天在迪士尼世界。 这很有趣, 但现在,教堂的栽培是乐趣,礼拜服务是乐趣,圣经研究是乐趣.

就像在二十英尺高的乔治亚松林中学习树木语言, 他们只是有趣的树。 他们并不伟大。 他们并不令人惊叹。 他们不会发抖。 他们只是有趣的树。

所以,诺亚, 增加你的喜悦和意义 和奇异的词汇, 因为比我们想承认的更多时候, 心脏收缩到 语言 我们必须表达它而不是相反。 如果你在不久之前就称它为“有趣”的话, 你的心会缩到词汇里 2. 知道你没有疯。

第二,听从圣经的警告, 圣经中非常了解那些不能快乐严肃的人,他们所有的语言都只是聪明或开玩笑,或三思而行. - 像个疯子

articles.content: On le surnomme l’ »Apôtre du Pérou ». Saint Toribio de Mogrovejo (1538-1606) était un archevêque espagnol, missionnaire au Pérou et deuxième évêque de Lima – territoire qui à l’époque englobait le nord du Pérou dont Chiclayo. Un prédécesseur, en quelque sort, de Mgr Robert Prevost ! En fin d’après-midi, le 14 novembre, Léon XIV a retrouvé la communauté catholique de son ancien diocèse de Chiclayo, au sanctuaire de Santo Toribio de Mogrovejo, à Zaña. En ce lieu où mourut saint Toribio, le Pape s’est recueilli devant son ancienne tombe – désormais vide puisque sa dépouille repose dans la cathédrale de Lima. Léon XIV a ensuite participé à la clôture de l’année jubilaire marquant le troisième centenaire de la canonisation du missionnaire espagnol. Né à Mayorga, en Espagne, saint Toribio étudie le droit et devient un juriste réputé, professeur à l’université de Salamanque. Alors qu’il est encore laïc, le roi Philippe II le désigne pour devenir archevêque de Lima. 他被誉为“秘鲁的使徒”。圣托里维奥·德·莫格罗韦霍（1538-1606）是一位西班牙大主教，曾是秘鲁的传教士，也是利马的第二任主教。利马当时管辖的领土包括秘鲁北部，其中就包括奇克拉约。在某种意义上，他是罗伯特·普雷沃斯特主教的前任！

11月14日下午晚些时候，利奥十四世在萨尼亚的圣托里维奥·德·莫格罗韦霍圣殿与他曾任主教的奇克拉约教区的天主教团体重聚。教宗在圣托里维奥逝世的这个地方，在其旧墓前默祷——该墓现已空置，因为他的遗体安葬在利马大教堂。

随后，利奥十四世参加了这位西班牙传教士封圣三百周年禧年的闭幕仪式。圣托里维奥出生于西班牙的马约尔加，他学习法律并成为一名著名的法学家，在萨拉曼卡大学任教。在他仍为俗人时，腓力二世国王任命他为利马大主教。

他接受了这一点。阅读全文……文章《圣托里比奥·德·莫格罗韦霍：激励良十四世的传教主教》最初发表于Aleteia。

articles.content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I like to let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. It is a quieter week than the last one, but it brings a revised edition of B. B. Warfield’s Biblical and Theological Studies, Alex Duke’s guided tour of Exodus (for which I provided a foreword), and two Crossway editions marking 500 years since William Tyndale’s English New Testament. On the academic side, you’ll find several noteworthy titles, including the New International Commentary on the Old Testament volume on Daniel 7–12. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. Books for Everyone Zondervan From Silence to Sinai A Guided Tour of Exodus Alex Duke Publisher’s description What adjectives would you use to describe the Bible? Inspired. Amazing. Unique. Authoritative. Perfect. Pure. Life-changing. Those descriptions are all deserved. Your pastors and parents and Sunday School teachers were right. There’s no book like God’s Book. Here’s another adjective: confusing. The Bible can be confusing, especially certain parts of the Old Testament. Moments after coming across something inspiring and encouraging, you’ll read something that makes you wonder, What is even happening right now!? The book of Exodus is no exception. This sequel to Genesis begins with God’s surprising silence. What a stark contrast to Genesis, where God’s words set everything in motion. It then tells the story of God’s miraculous liberation of his people, complete with frogs falling from the sky and life-saving blood being painted over doorways. Finally, for the last half of the book, the action slows down as the people of God gather at the mountain of God to receive the Law of God in order to engage in the worship of God. From silence to Sinai, that’s the story of Exodus. To understand it all, most of us will need a guide. We’ll need some help. That’s what From Silence to Sinai is for. Alex Duke walks readers through the book of Exodus to show that nothing in God’s story is wasted—not the silence, not the ten signs, and not even the confusing parts. In Exodus, God is not absent, random, or unclear. He is revealing himself, redeeming his people, and teaching them how to live in his presence. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . B&H The First Five Beating the Odds and Thriving as a Ministry Leader Kyle Worley and Joseph Worley Publisher’s description Is it possible to do more than survive in ministry leadership? Could you actually thrive? The alarming reality is that most ministry leaders will not make it more than five years in leadership. Burnout, lack of training, and an absence of coaches are all pitfalls on the road to sustainable ministry leadership. But there is a different roadmap for those willing to learn. In The First Five , Joseph and Kyle Worley present a pathway for thriving in ministry leadership. With over sixty years of experience, across churches of every size and shape, they provide a biblically rooted and tested approach to the personal, professional, and pastoral dynamics of ministry leadership. The First Five is designed to be a manual for new ministry leaders and those leading them. Don’t just read this book—use it! You can do more than survive as a ministry leader. We believe you can thrive. Buy it at Amazon . Preorder · releases Wednesday, November 11 P&R Biblical and Theological Studies Revised and Enhanced Benjamin B. Warfield, edited by John J. Hughes Endorsed by: Vern S. Poythress, Thomas R. Schreiner, R. Scott Clark, Donald Macleod, and Richard C. Gamble Publisher’s description Classic articles from Warfield, enhanced for ease of reading, explore God, predestination, the supernaturalism of Christianity, the antiquity and unity of the human race, mysticism, and the prophecies of Paul. 星期二是大多数出版商发布新书的一天, 所以我每个星期都想告诉你, 我最密切地关注的出版商 给我们带来了什么。 这周比上一周更安静,但带来了B. B.

沃菲尔德的圣经和神学研究,亚历克斯·杜克对Exodus的导游(我为此提供了前言),以及两个十字路口版,标志着威廉·廷达勒的"英语新约"(English New Tondament)以来的500年. 在学术方面,你会发现几个值得注意的标题,包括丹尼尔7-12上的旧约卷的新国际评注。

每一次,我都包括出版商的描述。 从沉默到西奈的图书, 你用什么形容词来形容圣经? 发菩提心. 厉害 独一无二 专权性. 不错 纯净. 改变生活。 这些描述都是值得的。 你的牧师和家长 以及星期日学校的老师是对的

没有像上帝的书那样的书。 以下是另一个形容词:令人困惑。 圣经可以令人困惑,特别是旧约中的某些部分. 在经历了一些鼓舞人心和鼓舞人心的事情之后, 你会读到一些让你感到奇怪的东西, 出家经卷亦无例外. 创世纪的续集开始于上帝令人惊讶的沉默。

与创世纪的鲜明对比,上帝的言语让一切动起来. 它讲述了上帝奇迹般地解放其人民的故事,最后是青蛙从天而降,在门道上画出拯救生命的鲜血。

最后,在书的后半段,随着上帝的百姓聚集在神的山上接受神的律法,以从事对神的崇拜,这一行动放缓了. 从沉默到西奈,这就是出埃及的故事。 为了了解这一切,我们大多数人都需要一个指南。 需要帮助。 从沉默到西奈,

亚历克斯·杜克(Alex Duke)通过《出神记》的书向读者表明,上帝的故事中没有任何东西是浪费的,不是沉默,不是十种迹象,甚至连令人困惑的部分也没有。 在出埃及语中,上帝不是缺席,是随意的,或者是不明确的. 他正在揭露自己,救赎他的人民,并教他们如何在他面前生活。 在亚马逊或威斯敏斯特书店买的

B&H 前5名击败奇数 并担任部领导 Kyle Worley 和 Joseph Worley 出版社的描述 在部委领导层中能否做更多的工作? 你真的能兴旺起来吗? 令人震惊的现实是,大多数部委领导人担任领导不超过五年。

燃烧、缺乏培训以及缺乏教练都是实现可持续部委领导道路上的陷阱。 但对于愿意学习的人,有不同的路线图。 在前五卷中,约瑟夫和凯尔·沃利提出了在部领导中蓬勃发展的途径。

具有60多年的经验,各种大小和形状的教会都对部委领导的个人、专业和牧业动态提供了具有圣经根源和考验的方法。 " 前五 " 旨在为新的部委领导人和领导者编写手册。 不要只读这本书, 作为部会领导,你可以做的不只是生存。

articles.content: Sonia Llauró de Ibarra en est convaincue : les vocations naissent au cœur des familles. Mère de douze enfants, dont six sont devenus prêtres et deux religieuses, elle sait combien une conversion peut transformer une famille. Pour cause, la sienne a commencé à l’âge de 18 ans, dans les premières années de son mariage avec Diego. Issue d’une famille catholique de Buenos Aires, en Argentine, elle a pourtant rencontré le Christ après avoir participé à une retraite ignatienne. Une conversion du cœur qui a progressivement transformé sa vie et, avec elle, celle de toute sa famille. « Si une personne n’est pas remplie de Dieu, elle ne peut rien donner », estime Sonia. Chapelet en famille, adoration du Saint-Sacrement, retraites spirituelles… Sonia et Diego ont élevé leurs enfants dans un environnement où la foi faisait partie intégrante du quotidien. Les fruits de cette éducation sont surprenants : deux de ses filles sont religieuses et six fils sont prêtres. Ils exercent leur ministère Tout lire… The post « Dieu les appelle pour qu’ils soient heureux » : le témoignage de Sonia, mère de huit consacrés appeared first on Aleteia .
articles.content_zh:
索尼娅·劳罗·德伊瓦拉 (Sonia Llauró de Ibarra) 坚信：职业是在家庭的心中诞生的。她是十二个孩子的母亲，其中六个成为牧师，两个成为修女，她知道皈依对一个家庭的改变有多大。她的婚姻始于 18 岁，也就是她与迭戈结婚的头几年，这是有充分理由的。

她来自阿根廷布宜诺斯艾利斯的一个天主教家庭，在参加伊格纳修静修会后遇到了基督。内心的转变逐渐改变了他的生活，也随之改变了他整个家庭的生活。 “如果一个人没有被神充满，他就无法给予任何东西，”索尼娅相信。

家庭念珠、崇拜圣体、精神静修……索尼娅和迭戈在信仰成为日常生活不可或缺的一部分的环境中抚养孩子。这种教育的成果令人惊讶：他的两个女儿是修女，六个儿子是牧师。

他们行使自己的事工 阅读全部... 帖子“神呼召他们，使他们快乐”：八个献身者的母亲索尼娅的见证首先出现在 Aleteia 上。

articles.title: Midlife Is a Crossroads, Not a Crisis
articles.summary: In ‘Good News for Midlife,’ Jared Wilson reminds us to embrace our midlife crossroads, find new meaning in service to others, and let this season be an opportunity to discover grace upon grace in Jesus.
articles.summary_zh: 在《中年好消息》（ Good News for Midlife ）一书中，贾里德·威尔逊（ Jared Wilson ）提醒我们要拥抱中年十字路口，寻找为他人服务的新意义，让这个季节成为在耶稣身上发现恩典的机会。
articles.title_zh: 中年是一个十字路口，而不是危机
articles.content: Last year, I was sitting with an early twentysomething grad student in our church. He said he was looking for an older man to mentor him, and I started thinking through our godly, wise men in their 50s and 60s. He stopped me and clarified: He was asking me to mentor him. “Wait, you think I’m old?!” I’m 42, and to be fair, I’ve been told I’m an “old soul” my whole life. Some have wondered aloud if I was born old. While I still don’t feel old, I’ll admit this new and strange season has spurred me to go looking for wisdom. I’ll tell you, reading about midlife is depressing. According to studies, happiness in life follows a U-shaped curve. Our self-reported happiness starts high in childhood, then decreases into adolescence and further into early adulthood. It bottoms out somewhere around age 46—smack in the center of middle age—before beginning to rise again and steadily increasing into our twilight years. Further, studies have shown that depression and anxiety also are highest around the age of 45. Despite all the bad news, Good News for Midlife: Navigating Middle Age with Guts and Grace was encouraging. Writing from his early 50s, Jared Wilson, associate professor of pastoral ministry at Midwestern Baptist Theological Seminary, understands the challenges of midlife but also provides refreshing hope for those of us finding our own way through. Understand Midlife Most definitions place “middle age” as 40 to 60, but it’s probably more accurate to describe midlife in terms of its demands and responsibilities. For me, it looks something like this: I still feel energetic, but it takes far longer to recover from lost sleep, injuries, and travel. My kids are now teenagers, and some days, I only see them for a half hour. Our grocery bill is three times our first mortgage. Our parents are in their 70s and now need more support from us than we need from them. I think I’m still in touch with modern culture, but my kids assure me I’m not. I may have 40-plus years left, but it sure feels like most of my life is now behind me. Most deeply, I’m frequently reflecting on life’s disappointments and griefs, wondering if I should have done this or that differently. This is middle life. We’re too young to feel old. But we’re also too old to feel young. Wilson, who writes specifically for men entering or inhabiting these decades, acknowledges all these challenges. “But,” he writes, “while this season presents unique challenges . . . midlife also presents exciting opportunities to trust Jesus for personal, marital, and spiritual flourishing” (xi). Thankfully, Wilson helps us reframe the demands and opportunities of middle age not as a necessary crisis but as a critical crossroads . Crossroads, Not Crisis For almost 60 years, pop culture has made “midlife” nearly synonymous with “crisis.” The phrase comes from psychoanalyst Elliott Jaques’s 1965 essay “ Death and the Mid-Life Crisis ” and has been repeated across dozens of books ever since. (There’s even a board game called Mid-Life Crisis, where players aim to accumulate wealth and avoid landing on bankruptcy, divorce, and nervous breakdown.) This is middle life. We’re too young to feel old. But we’re also too old to feel young. Fortunately, recent studies suggest fewer than 20 percent of Americans experience a full-on crisis in these middle decades. Despite this, many of us face a unique temptation to flee from responsibility or forge some entirely new life. Wilson puts it poignantly: “Whether you’re in a crisis or not, at midlife you’re at a crossroads” (16). At this crossroads, we see down one path the allure of individualism and freedom from responsibility. We might simply call this path the road of empty promises. As the proverbs say, it seems right, but in the end, it leads to death (Prov. 14:12). The second path is one of embracing reality, stepping deeper into relationship, and trusting the goodness of God. This road offers no promises other than the hardships of real life. But it’s also where

articles.title: Avoid the Trap of Bitterness
articles.summary: Joseph avoids the trap of bitterness. And you can too, if you follow these three steps.
articles.summary_zh: 约瑟避免了痛苦的陷阱。如果你遵循这三个步骤，你也可以这样做。
articles.title_zh: 避开苦涩的陷阱
articles.content: Imagine the people closest to you betray you. It’s your trust in them that lets them get close enough to hurt you so terribly. Now, imagine that this betrayal completely upends your life for years . Everything that made your life good—your family, your home, your safety—is violently taken from you. Now imagine years bleed into decades. Your life spirals into ever more pain and isolation. And every jab of hurt leads you to agonize over the initial wound: None of this would have happened if it weren’t for them. How could they do this? However, in the last few years, your fortunes have turned around. From the slums, you’re suddenly lifted to a vaulted position of power. People no longer take advantage of you but try to stay in your good graces. It doesn’t wash all the bitter memories away, but it’s something. And then, lo and behold, who happens to come before you but them . Your cruel betrayers are there, groveling, asking you for help. How would you feel? What would you do? If you haven’t picked up on it yet, this is the story of Joseph from Genesis. Sold into slavery by his brothers, Joseph walks through much injustice and suffering before being catapulted into the most powerful office in Egypt, second only to Pharaoh. And when his brothers come cringing toward him in the end, certain that Joseph will use his power to pay them back, Joseph responds with unexpected mercy, generosity, and warmth (Gen. 50:15–21) . How? Joseph avoids the trap of bitterness. And you can too, if you follow these three steps. 1. Understand Bitterness Bitterness is revealed in our emotions (coldness, anger, resentment, suspicion, revulsion), but it begins in our will. We choose bitterness when we believe that for justice or fairness to be preserved, the offender must be punished in some way. We may even claim to forgive, but in our heart of hearts, we fear that forgiveness comes at the expense of justice. So, you give your spouse the silent treatment, you cut your parents off, you make life difficult for your kids. Joseph avoids bitterness by trusting that God is the One who takes care of justice. When his brothers beg for mercy, Joseph replies, “Do not fear, for am I in the place of God?” (Gen. 50:19). Joseph knows it isn’t his place to deal out the judgment only God can give. The first step in avoiding bitterness is letting God take care of final justice (Rom. 12:14–21). Bitterness feels like a solution to the problem, but it isn’t. It’s trying to solve one sin with another sin. Which is why we’re commanded unequivocally to repent of bitterness, full stop (Eph. 4:31). We’re never told bitterness is an acceptable method to coerce repentance or pursue justice, or is permissible until the other person apologizes and makes restitution. Reconciliation requires two people who are willing. But to repent of bitterness only requires one. Bitterness feels like a solution to the problem, but it isn’t. It’s trying to solve one sin with another sin. Bitterness isn’t the path to justice—only to more bitterness. Using bitterness to pursue justice is like using a hatchet to build a house, confident it’ll work just like a hammer. 2. Unmask Bitterness We’re called to be so absolute and unqualified in rejecting bitterness because of its penchant to spread. It’s a “root” (Heb. 12:15) that will only grow and become more difficult to uproot as time goes on. Plucking up a sapling is easy; removing an oak tree isn’t. Soon, the bitterness you feel toward Person A will make you more prone to taking offense at Person B and more sensitive to Person C. Soon, you become an angry person who holds grudges. It’s a root that “defiles many.” Bitterness is hard to detect initially because it hides so effectively behind a mask of morality. The bitter person “blesses himself in his heart, saying, ‘I shall be safe, though I walk in the stubbornness of my heart’” (Deut. 29:19). In other words, “I’m not wrong, they are! They’re the ones who hurt me!” It not only immediately puts you into a

articles.title_zh: 神圣欢乐的味道
articles.content: Audio Transcript We like to think in simple categories. It’s easier that way, and easier to be clear in explaining things. So, if I ask, “How are you doing?” you will probably respond in terms of “good” or “bad,” and then explain why you are feeling good or bad. By default, we are doing fine until we are doing bad, but it’s normally one or the other, up or down like a light switch: We’re good. We’re bad. Then along comes the apostle Paul and pulls this on-off switch off the wall and breaks it into pieces to teach us that the very good and the very bad coexist in this life. Today on Ask Pastor John: the many flavors of holy joy. It’s a question from an anonymous listener to the podcast. “Pastor John, you have been writing and speaking for decades about the importance of joy in the life of God and the life of a Christian. You have made the case that joy in God — not only in his gifts but in his person — is essential to glorifying God. You have argued that the reason that God’s God-centeredness, his pursuit of his own glorification in all he does, is not megalomania is precisely because he magnifies his glory through our enjoyment of him. You have pointed out that the apostle Paul not only spoke of being ‘sorrowful, yet always rejoicing,’ but that he also said, ‘In all our affliction, I am overflowing with joy’ (2 Corinthians 6:10; 7:4). That last statement seems staggering. If it can be present in such different circumstances, can you help me even begin to imagine what true joy is?” Joy in All Circumstances That very statement from 2 Corinthians 7:4 has arrested my attention for a little over a year (since I taught 2 Corinthians last year) and just wouldn’t let me go, because it seems to demand that we dig into the nature of joy to figure out what he could possibly mean by calling his experience joyful in the light of so many different sufferings. He mentions 26 sufferings, different kinds of affliction in 2 Corinthians 11:23–28. It’s not just Paul’s experience of joy in all those afflictions that drives me, but many, many different circumstances in the Bible are the circumstances in which we are told to rejoice. It’s just incredible how many there are. Here are a few. - Rejoice in your future inheritance (1 Peter 1:3–6). - Rejoice that your names are written in heaven (Luke 10:20). - Rejoice in the plundering of your property for love’s sake (Hebrews 10:34). - Rejoice in being poured out for others (Philippians 2:17–18). - Rejoice in spending and being spent for souls (2 Corinthians 12:15). - Rejoice in your weakness for Christ’s sake (2 Corinthians 12:9–10). - Rejoice in being slandered and persecuted and rejected (Matthew 5:11–12; Luke 6:22–23). - Rejoice in being shamed for Christ’s name (Acts 5:41). - Rejoice in contributing to others’ needs (2 Corinthians 9:7). - Rejoice in the partnership of other believers (Philippians 1:4–5). - Rejoice in people being converted (1 Thessalonians 2:19–20). - Rejoice in the unity of believers (Philippians 2:2). - Rejoice in truth (1 Corinthians 13:6). - Rejoice in the law of God (Psalm 119:14, 111, 162). - Rejoice in the Lord (Philippians 4:4). - Rejoice in the hope of the glory of God (Romans 5:2). - Rejoice in God (Romans 5:11). That’s for starters. The variety of circumstances in which we are told to rejoice demands this: Joy is not a static emotion but one that changes in intensity. That’s pretty obvious for everybody, but also — this is what I’m drawing out now that feels fresh to me — it varies in quality. So, what do I mean by quality? I mean the nature or the kind of experience joy is — not just how intense it is but how different it is, or how it can feel so different from one kind of experience to the next. And yet, all of them could be called joy, which I think means a positive emotion that we really want to have. That would be my kind of bottom-line definition of joy. 音频记录 我们喜欢简单思考 这样比较容易, 因此,如果我问到“你在做什么?” 你可能会回答“好”或“坏”,然后解释你为什么感觉好或坏。 默认情况下,我们做得很好,直到我们做坏事为止,但通常它是一个或另一个,上或下像一个开关:我们很好。

我们是坏人。 然后使徒保罗来了 把这个关上 然后把它拆成碎片 教我们 生活中的善恶共存 今天在"问约翰牧师"(Ask Pastor John):许多圣乐的口味. 这是匿名听众对播客的提问。

“约翰神父,几十年来你一直在写作和谈论欢乐在上帝生活中的重要性和基督徒的生活。 你已说明,上帝的喜悦——不仅是他的礼物,而且是他个人的喜悦——对颂扬上帝至关重要。

你们认为,上帝的以神为本,他追求自己的美德,并不是因为大浪漫通过我们享受他的光荣。

你已指出使徒保罗不仅说出"悲伤而总是欢喜",他还说:"在我们所有的苦难中,我充满了欢快" (2 Corinthians 6: 10; 7: 4). 刚才的发言令人吃惊。

如果在这样不同的情况下它能够存在,你能帮助我开始想象真正的快乐是什么吗?” 所有情况下的欢乐 2个哥林多人7: 4的言论让我的注意力 一年多一点(因为去年我教过2个哥林多人),

在如此多不同痛苦的光芒下 称他的经历很快乐 他提到26起痛苦, 不仅仅是保罗在所有这些苦难中所经历的快乐, 这真是不可思议。

这里有一些。 - 享受你未来的遗产(1 Peter 1: 3-6) - 很高兴你们的名字写在天上(公爵10:20) - 在为爱而掠夺你的财产(赫布鲁斯10:34)中欢欣鼓舞. - 欢呼为他人倒出(菲利浦2:17-18)。 - 享受为灵魂而花和花的快乐(2科林斯人12:15).

- 为基督欢呼你的软弱(2科林斯人12:9-10). 被诽谤、迫害和拒绝(马修5:11–12;卢克6:22–23)。 - 乐于满足他人的需要(2科林斯9:7)。 - 与其他信徒合作欢呼(菲利浦1:4-5)。

- 很高兴有人被改造(1 Thessalonians 2:19-20)。 - 欢呼信徒的团结(菲利浦2:2). - 真理快乐(1科林斯13:6). - 在"上帝之法"中取悦("诗经"119:14,111,162). - 欢乐于主(菲利浦4:4). - 为上帝的荣耀而欢呼(罗马人5:2). - 享受上帝(罗马人5:11). 这首先要说明,

我们被告知欢乐的环境多种多样,这就要求我们:欢乐不是一种静态的情感,而是一种强度变化的情感. 这对每个人都是显而易见的,但同样——这是我现在所画的,我觉得很新鲜——它的质量也各不相同。 那么,我是什么意思 质量?

我指的是快乐的本质或体验类型——不仅仅是它有多强烈,而是它有多不同,或者它能有什么感觉,从一种体验到另一种体验如此不同. 然而,所有它们都可以叫做快乐, 我认为这意味着我们真正想要有一种积极的情感。 那就是我对快乐的底线定义

articles.content: Let me take a moment to remind you of some of the features of this site you may not know about. I have a growing page of Liturgies meant to help the local church in its worship. I also offer Book Recommendations across many categories and a list of the Best Commentaries for each book of the Bible. And if you like the quote graphics I share day by day, you can find them all at SquareQuotes.church where they are free to download. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several of the “Heart Talks” mini books that are meant to help women with common concerns: feeling like failures in parenting, husbands who lead poorly, doubt, and so on. You’ll also find Greg Gifford’s Lies My Therapist Told Me and several other titles. Recommended Reading Beer, Beef and Player’s Navy Cut. This is a brilliant article about C.S. Lewis and the vices that dogged him throughout his life—a three-pack-a day smoking habit, eating habits that bordered on gluttony, and far more alcohol than anyone should consume. “In case you really are new here and you mostly know Lewis from the kid’s books, let’s state the obvious: the man we universally honor as one of the 20th Century’s great saints smoked, ate and drank like he was a sponsored athlete of consumption. He sinned frequently through overindulgence. What do we do with this information?” How to Graciously Say No. You have probably run into the same conclusion I have: it’s often far harder to say no than to say yes. Yet sometimes the best thing we can do for ourselves and for others is to say no. Reagan Rose offers some thoughts on that (for those who have the ability to say no, of course, since in many occupations saying no isn’t an option). Can’t You Let Me Just Attend? “We live in a chronically noncommittal society. No wonder, then, that this has been dubbed the age of anxiety. Surely, covenant relationships aren’t the only cure, but it might surprise us how much stability of soul comes from deep, reliable, unflighty fellowship.” David Mathis explains why commitment to a particular church is so important, even if it’s extremely countercultural. When Morningness Is Confused With Godliness. I always enjoy an article that provides an alternate view of something we almost take for granted. That’s the case with this one from Cole Mizel, who is concerned that we may be too quick to imply that the best Christians do their daily devotions in the morning. “But is it really more virtuous to be a morning person than a night owl?” Everyone Doesn’t React the Same Way. J.V. Fesko makes a simple but wise point here: everyone doesn’t respond to preaching the same way. Because that’s the case, we should not assume that those who display a lot of emotion are necessarily being impacted more than those who do not. “Tears are not the sacrament of a changed heart, the visible sign and seal of an anguished and healed soul.” Evangelising With a Dog. I enjoyed reading Peter Barnes’s account of evangelizing with a dog. “My doctor, who is half my size, suggested as tactfully as he could, what was obvious to all – that my squash days were over, and that I should take to walking the dog in the morning and at lunchtime. So this has become my nod to the need for daily exercise. Being one of the few beings on the planet who still buys a hard copy of a daily newspaper, I take my hound – a cocker spaniel with unusually short legs – with me of a morning. On the way, on most days at least, we pass a stand where two, sometimes three, Jehovah’s Witness ladies seek to engage people in conversation.” New Book Releases New Christian books tend to release on Tuesdays. Here are just a few of the books that have become available today. For a more thorough list—and there are several more than I have listed here—visit This Week in Christian Books .
